name: Google Fonts
summary: Hosted webfont service: the standard way to pull a typeface into a user project with two link tags, no npm dependency.
license: Fonts carry their own licenses, mostly OFL; the service is free to use

steps: Put two preconnect hints before the stylesheet link: one for fonts.googleapis.com, one crossorigin for fonts.gstatic.com (that is where the woff2 bytes live).
Then the css2 stylesheet link with the family and weight axis you need, and display=swap so text paints on a fallback rather than hiding.
Wire the family into Tailwind v4 with an @theme block: --font-sans: "Inter", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif.
Self-hosted alternative with no runtime request to Google: the fontsource entry.

files.role: Preconnect plus stylesheet link, the complete Google Fonts wiring
files.content:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
<link
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@100..900&display=swap"
  rel="stylesheet"
/>

files.role: Point Tailwind v4's font-sans at the loaded family

notes: Scope of the offline rule: this repo's gallery, templates, and authored files never reference Google Fonts (the design-template-authoring skill bans it and the frontend build rewrites such imports to local vendor copies). The user's project is different: when they want Google Fonts, this is the correct wiring. Typography pairing guidance lives in references/typography.md. Variable-axis URLs use the axis@range syntax shown here; non-variable families list discrete weights.
